headline: Generative protein models conditioned on properties, structure, and sequence context
label: Context Conditioned Protein Modeling
summary: Recent work conditions pretrained protein and RNA generative models on explicit properties and structural alignment, moving beyond sequence-only design.
synthesis: The dominant thread is generative sequence design that draws on explicit context rather than sequence alone. ProteinGuide adds on-the-fly conditioning on auxiliary properties to pretrained protein sequence models (ESM3, ProteinMPNN, MultiFlow). AlignIF applies structure-alignment-driven cross-graph modeling to RNA sequence design and reports functional fluorescent aptamers. Raygun takes a distributional route, encoding proteins as fixed-dimension probability distributions over language model embeddings to miniaturize and modify natural proteins. What appears new is treating property or structural context as an explicit control layered onto existing generative models. The set is heterogeneous: only AlignIF addresses nucleic acids, and Raygun differs by operating through a distributional representation rather than an added property input, so the shared thread is dominant rather than universal.
